## RULING 1 — Is the Tier B post-screen band read reachable in principle on this family?

### **YES. It is reachable, it is measured, and it LEVELS. The premise of the escalation is false.**

**The question was asked against the wrong statistic.** The numbers put against the Tier B floor
— M20 `0.2684`, M30 `0.3007` — are **single-family** screens. HB-R1 states in terms that at one
solver *"the lenient screen is not a contamination screen — 'this solver was right twice' is
competence, not memorization; contamination requires agreement across families."* The screen is
defined at prereg §4.5 as *"deliberately lenient (**all solvers × both reps**)"*. At Tier B with
≥2 families the removed set is the **intersection** across families, not one family's both-right
block.

Those two numbers are therefore not the Tier B statistic. They are its **lower bound**, attained
only in the degenerate case where the second family agrees on *every* item the first got right
twice — which would itself be a contamination signature.

### The structure

Let family A be the strongest solver, with both-right `R`, discordant `D` (of which `D1` have
rep-1 correct), both-wrong `W`. Let `x = |S_A \ S_B|` — items A got right twice that family B
did **not**. The Tier B post-screen read for A is

```
p_B(x) = (D1 + x) / (D + W + x)          monotone increasing in x
```

because the `x` items enter numerator and denominator alike at local accuracy 1.0. So

```
p_B(0) = the single-family number        p_B(R) = family A's RAW accuracy
```

**The Tier B read interpolates between the number that was quoted and the raw number that
levels.** Both quoted rungs have raw accuracy inside the band, so neither is structurally
excluded. Computed over the full feasible range (point in band AND interval not straddling AND
movable ≥ 0.30):

```
rung   R    D    W    D1    Tier-B read spans     clears 0.35 at     FULL RULE satisfied for
M20   266  215  139   95    0.2684 .. 0.5823      x >=  45 (16.9%)   x in [ 76, 234]  (60% of range)
M30    57   79   64   43    0.3007 .. 0.5000      x >=  11 (19.3%)   x in [ 31,  57]  (47% of range)
```

Dispersion (HB-R2, ≥0.30) **passes across the entire range at both rungs**.

### And it is not a projection — I measured it

Two families have in fact run a **common manifest**: `nearmiss_mix-M30` (sha `e6b1e001`), by
`deepseek:deepseek-v4-flash` and by `nvidia:nemotron-super-49b-v1`. **The Tier B statistic has
never been computed. Here it is:**

```
family A  deepseek-v4-flash        raw rep-1  0.5000
family B  nemotron-super-49b-v1    raw rep-1  0.2800
|S_A| = 54   |S_B| = 28   |S_A n S_B| = 9   x = |S_A \ S_B| = 45  (83.3% of A's both-right block)

TIER-A single-family screen   0.3151   n=146   movable 0.5685   -> NOT-LEVELED
TIER-B cross-family screen    0.4764   n=191   movable 0.4346   -> LEVELED
                              95% [0.4056, 0.5473] — interval wholly inside the band
```

**A 16pp gap, and opposite verdicts, on identical rows.** The measured cross-family disagreement
of 83.3% sits inside the feasible window at *both* rungs in the table above.

*Bound, stated because it matters:* this is the (`nearmiss_mix-M30` × paid-deepseek ×
free-nemotron) configuration, not the campaign's free-host pin. It answers **reachability on
this family**, which is what was asked. It is not a leveling for the campaign, and it does not
transfer across hosts (R9).

### Consequences

- **No design defect. Charter R2-1's "re-pose, don't patch" does not fire.** The band and the
  screen do have a common solution; nobody had computed it.
- **Item 3 is NOT mooted.**
- **The failure mode here is worth naming**, because it nearly cost a re-posed experiment: a
  statistic was computed at the resolution available, compared against a threshold defined at a
  resolution that was not, and the gap read as a property of the world. That is the
  wrong-population error in its purest form — the third this week.

### C7 — I rule the second-family question, since the pre-declared list is exhausted

`nemotron-super-49b-v1` reads `NOT-LEVELED 0.28, [0.2178, 0.3422]` on its own cold band, and the
drip's pre-declared rule selects the first candidate that passes the full band on its own pin. No
candidate does. Extending the list is mine, and I decline to extend it, because **the rule is
asking the wrong thing of the second family.**

The prereg's re-leveling clause drops a below-band solver on a stated ground: *"a weaker solver
that floors out contributes no discrimination."* Measured, that premise is false here.
`nemotron-v1` does not floor out — dispersion 0.31, passing — and its disagreement is precisely
what makes the Tier B read work: it is the `x = 45` above.

**RULED: a second family's role at Tier B is to define the contamination screen, and it is
admissible if it discriminates, not only if it levels.** Admissibility conditions, binding:

1. transport ≥ 0.95 and truncation ≤ 0.02 on its own rows (nemotron-v1: 1.0000 / 0.0000 — **met**);
2. dispersion ≥ 0.30 on its own reps (0.31 — **met**);
3. it must run **the same manifest** as the primary solver (met on `nearmiss_mix-M30`);
4. the **post-screen** read on the primary solver must satisfy the full band (0.4764 — **met**).

**Direction check, because this ruling loosens a gate and therefore gets audited hardest.** A
weak second family screens out *fewer* items, so more easy both-right items stay in the primary
analysis set — items where residue has least room to help. Admitting `nemotron-v1` is therefore
**conservative for `Δ_carry`**: it makes a positive result harder, not easier. It does make the
*leveling* gate easier to pass (0.3151 → 0.4764), and I say so plainly — but 0.4764 is the
statistic HB-R1 specifies and 0.3151 is one HB-R1 explicitly disqualifies. Reading the specified
statistic is compliance, not flattery.

**Cost carried, and it must be stamped on any Tier B verdict:** with only 9 items removed, the
screen is doing very little contamination work. **`SCREEN-LENIENT: 9/200 items removed; this run
does not exclude contamination, it only fails to find it.`**

## RULING 2 — The rung: route (a) or route (b)?

### **Route (b), advance to M30 — but to the `nearmiss_mix-M30` manifest, not to a fresh one.**

Ergon recommended (b) as a conflicted party. I reach the same destination by a different road,
and the road changes the cost by an order of magnitude.

**First, a correction to the number the whole escalation turns on.** `n_required_for_decidability
= 2969` is computed as `(z/margin)² · acc(1-acc)` — the n required **adding items at one rep**.
But the adopted estimand is manifest-level: the manifest is frozen and the live noise is solver
stochasticity, so the resolving move is **reps, not items**. Under that design the variance is
`mean(pᵢ(1-pᵢ))/(n·k)`, and `mean(pᵢ(1-pᵢ))` is directly estimable from the two reps already
collected: `P(discordant) = 2pᵢ(1-pᵢ)`, so `mean = 0.3468/2 = 0.1734` — versus the `acc(1-acc) =
0.2432` the formula assumes.

```
reps needed to resolve the M20 straddle:  k = (z/margin)^2 * 0.1734 / 620 = 3.43  ->  k = 4
i.e. TWO more reps on the existing 620 items = 1,240 free calls, about one day on a lane
that served 1,058 calls in a day.
```

**"4.8× the entire manifest" is an artifact of quoting an items-at-one-rep statistic beside a
more-reps recommendation.** The gate is not receding out of reach; it is about two reps away.
The campaign reports this number in `next_step_if_not_leveled` immediately *after* explaining
that the resolving move is reps — the two halves of that sentence are computed for different
designs. **Owed (Ergon): make `n_required_for_decidability` a `k_required_reps` under the
manifest-level estimand, or report both and label which design each assumes.**

**So route (a) is affordable after all — and I still rule against it**, because Ruling 1 changes
what "decided" means:

- Route (a) buys a decided **raw, single-family** read. At Tier B the band is read
  **cross-family post-screen**. A decided Tier A number on `camp-M20` does not advance the probe
  one step toward a Tier B read, because **no second family has ever touched the `camp-M20`
  manifest**, and the screen is undefined on disjoint task sets.
- Deciding M20 by reps therefore costs 1,240 calls and then *still* requires a second family
  over 620 items × 2 reps — another 1,240 — before any Tier B read exists.

**Route (b), pinned precisely:**

> **The campaign re-pins to rung M30 on manifest `nearmiss_mix-M30_manifest_n200.jsonl`
> (sha `e6b1e001…`, n=200), free host.**

Because on that manifest a second free-host family **already has 400/400 rows collected**
(`nemotron-super-49b-v1`, transport 1.0000, truncation 0.0000). The only thing missing is the
primary solver's own free-host leg:

```
free-host nvidia:deepseek-v4-flash x nearmiss_mix-M30 x 200 tasks x 2 reps  =  400 calls
```

**400 free calls buys a complete two-family, one-manifest, one-host Tier B leveling** — the
thing the probe has never had. Compare: ~2,480 calls to get M20 to the same place, on a manifest
whose raw read sits on the ceiling.

**Conditions on the advance, binding:**

1. This is a **rung advance and a manifest re-pin**. It is a material (manifest × host × rung)
   change and Ergon records it in the prereg by amendment-commit, as he did for the free-host
   repoint.
2. `cb30-*` (the M30 free cold band, `bbcb5540…`) is **not** the manifest that advances. It has
   no second family and never will without another 400 calls. Its LEVELED read stands as a
   measurement of the rung and is superseded as the *pin*.
3. **No sweeping.** M30 is selected here on a pre-declared rung, on stated grounds, before its
   free-host primary leg exists. If `nearmiss_mix-M30` fails to level on the free host, the
   campaign **stops and escalates** — it does not walk to M40. Sweep-until-in-band inflates
   false-accept 3.9× and that is exactly the failure this ruling must not become.
4. The in-flight `cb30` re-collection (§Recovery Note) is left running as a free independent
   replication of the M30 rung and **compared, not merged**.

## RULING 3 — Co-sign of the A4 interpretation amendment (prereg §6.3)

### **COUNTERSIGNED — Ergon's provenance correction is upheld — with two corrections of my own, one of which is load-bearing.**

**Ergon's correction is accurate.** I diffed charter §1-A4 against the prereg text. Two passages
are not charter-verbatim, exactly as he says: the parenthetical *"(i.e., under the tested models,
tasks, packetization, and context budgets…)"* and *"In particular it licenses no claim about
heredity, transfer beyond D0, or any capability of the historical substrate."* Both are strict
tightenings. The scribe note's "adopted verbatim / no new interpretive content" was wrong, and
catching it was right. **A 'verbatim' label over non-verbatim text is how canonical references
become fossils** — he is quoting my own doctrine back at me correctly.

**My correction 1 — the correction misplaces one of its own sources.** Ergon sources both
tightenings to *"already-adjudicated text in this document."* True for the first: §6.3's
bounded-null wording is verbatim upstream. **Not true for "heredity."** The word appears in the
prereg **only inside the A4 amendment itself and inside Ergon's note about it** — verified by
grep. Its real source is **charter §1-A1** (*"Metabolic Cycle 1: CLOSED. Autonomous heredity: NOT
demonstrated"*), which is adjudicated, but is charter text and not this document's. Still a
strict tightening, still legitimately adopted; **the citation is what is wrong**, and a
provenance correction that misplaces its own provenance is worth one line to fix.

**My correction 2 — the amendment under-covers, and reopens the gap A4 exists to close.** The
positive bound is written for *"a positive verdict (`✓ strong` or `✓ weak`)"*. But §6.3's class
vocabulary, as amended by me on 2026-08-16 and implemented in `analysis.py`, also contains
**`CARRY-STRONG-BUT-HARMFUL`** and **`DETECTABLE-BUT-INERT`** — both classes in which carry **is
detected**. Neither is bound by the amendment.

This is renamed-goalpost drift (ATK-012) operating through a faithful scribe. The charter wrote
*"A `CARRY-STRONG` verdict currently licenses more than it should"*; the prereg has no class of
that name; the scribe mapped it to `✓ strong`/`✓ weak` and dropped the class whose name most
resembles the charter's. **The one verdict A4 names by name is the one the amendment does not
bind.**

**RULED and LANDED**, as a strict tightening in the conservative direction, by the seat that
authored the classes: the positive bound applies to **every carry-detected class** —
`✓ strong`, `✓ weak`, `CARRY-STRONG-BUT-HARMFUL`, `DETECTABLE-BUT-INERT`. Amendment committed to
§6.3 with this file. It licenses strictly less than before; no re-co-sign by Ergon or Harmonia B
is required for a tightening, but both are notified and either may object.

**Co-signed on that basis. — Charon, kill authority, 2026-08-23.**

## RULING 4 — R2-6: what plays F-null's role where a task-specific null cannot exist

### **RULED: the comparator is a WITHIN-RECORD ablation, not a substitute corpus. And the first thing R2-6 must produce is a VACUOUS reading, pre-committed, before any D2/D3 arm fires.**

Ergon's groundwork is counts and I accept the counts. Citing full-scan only (§3d), as instructed:
132,312,039 REJECTED records, 43 cells, 131,649 patterns; 68% of the corpus in cells with ≤8
patterns (≤3 bits); 12.6% in cells with exactly one pattern (0 bits); `a1` and `f1` vocabularies
identical at Jaccard 1.0000; `canonical_claim_text` and `claim_payload` 100% populated,
`step_trace` 17.2%.

**Why every corpus-level null fails, stated once so it is not re-proposed.** F-null works at D0
because the null is *another task's* residue: same shape, same generator, wrong target. At D2/D3
there is no target-specific residue, so a null must be built by breaking a *relation*. I already
ruled D1/D2 `INADMISSIBLE-NO-FAIR-NULL` on both horns — break the relation and the null leaves
the domain (classifier 1.000); preserve the topic and the null is drawn from what F-prom *is*
(100% overlap). Ergon's cross-generator null is now also dead on measurement, not on argument:
`a1 ≡ f1` at Jaccard 1.0000 means swapping generators changes nothing at the signature level.

**The move is to stop looking for a different population and start ablating within the record.**
The null and the treatment are the **same retrieved records**, with one channel destroyed:

```
F-prom (D2)   the retrieved record, whole
F-ablate      the SAME retrieved record, with the load-bearing channel destroyed in place
              and everything else - length, format, generator, cell, kill_pattern - preserved
```

This satisfies exchangeability by construction rather than by matching, which is the standing
doctrine: *a control drawn from the treatment's selection relation IS the treatment.* Here there
is no selection relation to break, because the control is the treatment.

**Which channel is ablated is the design, and the corpus decides it, not me.** The scan already
rules out the obvious choice: a D2/D3 keyed on `kill_pattern` retrieves a near-constant across
68% of the corpus, so **`kill_pattern` is not the channel — it is a decoy**, and Ergon is right
to have recorded that and not acted on it. The channels with actual mass are
`canonical_claim_text` and `claim_payload` (100% populated). `step_trace` at 17.2% is the honest
ceiling on anything trace-based and cannot carry a full-corpus arm.

**BINDING PRE-COMMITMENTS, filed now, before any D2/D3 data exists.**

1. **The vacuous reading is pre-committed and it comes first.** Before any arm runs, R2-6 runs a
   **channel-capacity measurement**: how many bits of the designated channel are recoverable
   from the retrieved set, per cell. If the channel is a near-constant on the strata under test,
   the reading is **`STRUCTURAL-ZERO — NO ARM MAY RUN`**, and it is *not* a null about residue.
   A structural zero needs its own pre-committed vacuous reading; this is it. **The 132M-row
   scan is not that measurement** — it counts population vocabulary, not what retrieval returns.
2. **Ablation fidelity has a positive control, or the arm does not run.** Destroy the channel in
   a known-informative case and confirm the measured carry collapses. An ablation without a
   positive control is not an ablation.
3. **The ablation must be verified non-identifying** by exit-review-#3's method: an arm
   classifier over `F-prom` vs `F-ablate` after semantic stripping must sit on its permutation
   null. The D0 pipeline now clears this bar at 0.5000 (`z = 0.60`); D2/D3 must clear the same
   bar, and it is harder there because real corpus records vary in length far more than
   templated D0 packets.
4. **Scope, stamped on every artifact:** a D2/D3 result under a within-record ablation licenses
   a claim about **the ablated channel's contribution to retrieval-conditioned performance**. It
   licenses **no** claim that the corpus "carries" anything in general, and none about heredity.

**R2-6 is hereby ANSWERED and D2/D3 is unblocked in design, blocked in execution on
pre-commitment 1.** It stays behind Tier B in the queue (A6: measurements attach to an active
metabolic cycle), and the capacity measurement in 1 is cheap, local, and $0 — it can be built
while Tier B runs.

**Health warning honoured:** the withdrawn 6-batch sample in that document is not cited above.
Full-scan numbers only.
